problem: The compact panel used native backdrop glass, but the expanded workspace introduced separate dark surfaces and did not preserve the same visual effect across the full window.
solution: A single edge-to-edge UnifiedTriosGlassBackground now sits behind the complete application hierarchy. Native full-screen material, a restrained contrast wash, and stable ambient color blooms remain visible beneath the title bar, tabs, history sidebar, and conversation in every width mode.
lesson: Window-wide visual effects should live above adaptive layout decisions. A shared transparent background prevents compact and expanded modes from drifting while deterministic tint blooms preserve identity in isolated macOS full-screen Spaces.
